title: Proper direct image preserves ordinary finite-coefficient bounded constructibility over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $f:Y\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites and their derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then for every $L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], one has $Rf_*L\in D^b_c(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Neither scheme is assumed to have finite Krull dimension. No invertibility condition on $A$ on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GL0, theorem-constructible-shriek, with the identity-open compactification for proper f; boundedness from literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 095U, lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper. This is the proper-finiteness input used in ILO XIII Proposition 3.4.2.

proof.text: Both schemes have finite affine covers by hypothesis, so are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. They are locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $f$ is separated, quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Since $S$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation. Its separatedness implies quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]; together with quasi-compactness this is finite presentation as defined in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Thus the qcqs and finite-presentation hypotheses of the constructibility theorem hold.

source.place: Tag 01TX, lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation; properties.tex Tags 01OV and 01OY (locally Noetherian and quasi-separated)

proof.text: Choose integers $a\leq b$ with $\mathcal H^r(L)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ and all $\mathcal H^r(L)$ constructible, using [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For the proper map $f$, take the identity compactification $(j,p)=(1_Y,f)$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Every object of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ factors uniquely through $1_Y$, so the presheaf defining $(1_Y)_!F$ in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is exactly the already sheafified $F$, including its restriction maps. Consequently $(1_Y)_!$ is the identity termwise and the compactification candidate is $Rf_*L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compactification-constructibility] to this candidate and the bounded-below complex $L$: every $\mathcal H^q(Rf_*L)$ is constructible. The cited theorem allows any finite commutative coefficient ring, with no invertibility hypothesis.

The morphism $f$ is of finite type and $S$ is quasi-compact by Step 1. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to obtain one integer $d\geq0$ bounding the dimensions of all scheme-theoretic fibres $Y_s$. This is a bound for the fibres only, and does not require finite Krull dimension of $Y$ or $S$. Empty fibres are permitted by the cited statement.

For any ordinary $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion: finiteness of $A$ gives integers $i<j$ with $i1_A=j1_A$, so $N=j-i>0$ satisfies $N1_A=0$ and kills every local section of every $A$-module. By [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound], the abelian higher direct images vanish for $q>2d$. The comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies these with the underlying abelian sheaves of the module higher direct images. A module sheaf whose underlying abelian sheaf is zero is zero, so $\mathcal H^q(Rf_*(M[0]))=0$ for $q>2d$ also with $A$-module coefficients. The categories of module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and $f_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] gives vanishing for $q<0$. Altogether $Rf_*(M[0])$ has cohomology only in $[0,2d]$, including when $A$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 095U, lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 03FD and 072W; derived.tex Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing

proof.text: The module categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] to their additive left exact direct image from Step 4: $Rf_*$ preserves distinguished triangles and commutes with shifts on $D^+$. For $a\leq r\leq b$, use the successive triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], with terms $\tau_{\leq r-1}L$, $\tau_{\leq r}L$, and $\mathcal H^r(L)[-r]$. The first truncation $\tau_{\leq a-1}L$ is zero, since all its cohomology is zero. Step 4 and [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] put the image of the third term in degrees $[r,r+2d]\subseteq[a,b+2d]$. Inductively, if the image of the first term has cohomology zero outside $[a,b+2d]$, exactness of $\mathcal H^q$ of the three terms from [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] forces the same for the middle term. This proves the claim for every $r$ through $b$; since $\tau_{\leq b}L\simeq L$, $Rf_*L$ has cohomology only in $[a,b+2d]$. Together with Step 2 and the definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], this proves $Rf_*L\in D^b_c(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.
